ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kokoro wa, nanika ga arimasu)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. But as the networks get bigger and more complex, it becomes really hard to understand what's going on inside, you see? (Muzukashii desu)

It's like trying to describe a beautiful painting to someone who's never seen it before. You can point to the colors and shapes, but you can't fully capture the magic of how it all comes together, ne? (Nan desu ka?)

The creators of these networks are like, "Hey, this thing is working, but I have no idea how it's doing it!" (Muzukashii desu) And that's okay, because sometimes the best way to understand something is to just use it and see what happens, you know? (Kokoro wa, nanika ga arimasu)

So, even though the creators don't fully understand how these networks work, they're still really good at using them to solve problems and create cool stuff, like chatbots and art generators! (Sugoi desu!)
